en.title: HushBook – Read while listening
en.summary: HushBook is an audiobook read-along app built for readers with ADHD, dyslexia, or poor reading comprehension. It plays the audiobook files you already own and…
en.body:
Published 10 September 2026 by HushBook

HushBook is an audiobook read-along app built for readers with ADHD, dyslexia, or poor reading comprehension. It plays the audiobook files you already own and highlights every word in sync with the narration, so the eye and ear stay locked together. Fully on-device: offline, no account, no ads, free on Android and iOS, with about 20,000 public-domain titles included.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The core accessibility feature is word-by-word highlighting synced to the narrator's voice, designed for readers who struggle to follow text alone or audio alone. Everything works offline with no account required. Screen-reader testing is ongoing and we welcome feedback from blind and low-vision users at hello@hushbook.app.

es.title: Accesibilidad y Tecnología Vive el fútbol accesible con Movistar Touch en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.summary: Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.body:
Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Se trata de Movistar Touch , un servicio gratuito dirigido a aficionados con entrada para el encuentro, que permite seguir el desarrollo del partido mediante audiodescripción y una tableta háptica capaz de reproducir en tiempo real la posición del balón sobre el terreno de juego. Esta tecnología ofrece una nueva forma de vivir la emoción del fútbol y constituye un excelente ejemplo de cómo la innovación puede contribuir a derribar barreras y favorecer la participación de todas las personas.

Actualmente, el Riyadh Air Metropolitano es el único estadio de España que ofrece este sistema. Las personas afiliadas interesadas en utilizarlo deberán solicitarlo previamente enviando un correo electrónico a inclusion@atleticodemadrid.com , indicando el partido de LALIGA para el que desean adquirir entradas y hacer uso del servicio.

Es importante tener en cuenta que Movistar Touch dispone de un número limitado de unidades, por lo que se recomienda realizar la solicitud con la mayor antelación posible.

Esta iniciativa se enmarca en la colaboración que el Atlético de Madrid mantiene desde hace años con la ONCE y Fundación ONCE para seguir mejorando la accesibilidad de sus instalaciones y servicios, reforzando así su compromiso con un deporte más inclusivo y accesible para todos.

en.title: Surprise and Shine: Recapping Apple's September 9 Announcements
en.summary: Intro Apple has just wrapped up Surprise and Shine, the big fall announcement event. We got new iPhones, Apple Watches, and (non-pro) AirPods. And yes, the rumors were finally true: one of the new iPhones is a folding one. AirPods have some new tricks, the new Apple Watch has some very nice improvements, and even the normal iPhones are worth checking out. Let's get into it. iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo All of the iPhones announced today share a few features, so we'll start there. At the heart of each new iPhone is the A20 Pro, a system on a chip (SoC) that's better than anything Apple has ever made. So said the presenters, anyway. This is Apple's first 2NM chip, which basically means they shrank the parts so they can fit more into the same amount of space, all while using less power and producing less heat. The A20 Pro comes with four efficiency cores and two cores meant to do serious work, which is the same distribution as last year (six cores, with four efficiency and two powerful ones). The big change here is that the two workhorse cores, called super cores, are beefed up considerably. Apple claims they have desktop performance. The graphics chip has also been upgraded, with seven cores and faster access to the phone's RAM; Apple says graphics run up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro. It's 2026, so we can't not talk about AI, specifically large language models. The A20 Pro has neural accelerators to boost AI performance for the CPU and GPU cores, but the star of the show is the neural engine. Or rather, the engines, plural. Each A20 Pro has two of them, not just one, giving the chip 32 neural cores to work with. Combined with the A20's increased access to memory, Apple said that this is the best chip for mobile AI tasks. All of this performance is going to produce a lot of heat, so Apple took the vapor chamber from iPhone 17 Pro and made some improvements. The way the chip's components transfer heat to the chamber is more efficient now, the materials have been updated, and the design has been altered. The new design has three times the space and is made from a combination of titanium and a special copper alloy. It transfers 40% more heat than the system on iPhone 17 Pro, letting the phone do more work for longer before it has to slow itself down to keep from overheating. Remember Siri AI, a version of Siri that is aware of your locations, messages, and other details? It was announced back in June. If you don't follow Apple news as obsessively as I do, the short version is that Siri is far more aware and capable than before. You can ask for "that recipe Jake sent me a couple months ago", you can issue more natural commands, and you can get much more accurate results with dictation. All of this is kept in a new Siri app, so you can check on past conversations. Oh, and Siri's voice is better than ever. Anyway, Siri AI is fully supported by all the new phones, and Apple spent some time reminding us of what all is going to be possible. There are some extra goodies for Apple Watch Series 12 owners who have Siri AI devices, too, but we'll get to those later. iPhone 18 Pro As has become customary, Apple is offering this year's pro phones in standard and Max variants. The Max has the most battery life of any iPhone ever, while the smaller phone has battery life equivalent to what iPhone 17 Pro Max offers. This seems to be the main difference; both have the same chip, camera, design, and everything else, so I'll just talk about iPhone 18 Pro from here on out. Everything also applies to iPhone 18 Pro Max unless I say otherwise. The stand-out feature of the camera system this year is variable aperture. Specially-designed, tiny pieces in the camera can move to let in more or less light, which also changes the field depth. The aperture widens in low light, closes some in bright light, and can be manually adjusted to change the feel of a picture. I guess professional photographers will be jumping for joy. The A20 Pro's AI capabilities also allow Apple to add more camera enhancements, some of which we knew about already from the iOS 27 announcement at WWDC back in June. What is unique to iPhone 18 Pro, though, is a new set of manual camera controls, called pro controls. These let you change the aperture, white balance, and other settings whose purpose I can only guess at. You can even use AI to keep video locked on a subject. But you're not here for camera details, so let's get on with it. There are a few other, smaller changes compared to iPhone 17 Pro. The new phone can charge faster when plugged in (as opposed to using wireless charging). The Dynamic Island is also smaller and now supports up to three live activities at once. Surprisingly, that's about it. The battery life improvements are great, the A20 Pro sounds like an impressive chip, and the colors have changed (silver, black, glacier, and burgundy). Aside from that, faster wired charging, and the camera improvements, everything seems to be the same. Apple didn't mention the screen, body material, any new or changed buttons, speakers, wifi performance, or anything else. It seems iPhone 18 Pro is, physically, the same as iPhone 17 Pro, just with a new chip and camera. You can pre-order iPhone 18 Pro starting September 12, and it will start shipping on September 18. The Pro starts at $1,199, $1,299 for the Pro Max. This gives you 256GB of storage, just like last year. You can upgrade all the way up to 2TB of storage, the first time any iPhone has offered such a large internal drive. Just know that it won't be cheap. You can also check out the new array of colors for Apple's official cases, cross-body straps, and (new this year) wrist straps. iPhone Duo Apple's first entry into the world of foldable phones is called iPhone Duo . It has a 5.4-inch outer display and unfolds to show a 7.6-inch screen. Both screens have full Apple Pencil support, and the outer screen has Ceramic Shield 2. The frame is high-grade titanium, colored either white or night sky. The side button acts how you expect, but also sports a Touch ID sensor--the phone lacks Face ID. You can add multiple fingers, so that no matter how you happen to hold the phone, the finger resting on the button can unlock it. You can also unlock your phone with your watch. Also, despite being foldable, iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating. That means dust and water will have a hard time getting into it, but you shouldn't take it swimming. Each half of iPhone Duo is very, very thin--after all, the whole package has to be comfortably thin when folded. Apple says that each half is the thinnest iPhone ever produced, which suggests that the halves are thinner than an iPhone Air. Despite this, iPhone Duo has good battery life (30 hours of video playback on the internal screen, 44 when using the outer one) and supports fast wired charging. It also, as mentioned earlier, has the same A20 Pro chip and vapor chamber cooling as iPhone 18 Pro. It even has Apple's custom cellular modem, the C2, giving it millimeter wave 5G support (U.S. only for now) and faster and more efficient cellular communications overall. The camera situation is interesting. iPhone Duo sports the same camera system as iPhone 18 Pro, though without the variable aperture feature. When unfolded, an under-screen selfie camera is available, while a more capable camera lives just above the outer screen. This enables some neat options, such as letting both the photographer and the subject see the camera feed (one person on the inner screen, the other on the outer one) before a picture is taken. If you are taking pictures of children, iOS lets you enable animations designed to draw attention and get the kids' eyes looking toward the lens. When making FaceTime calls, someone can use the inner camera and screen, while someone else can use the outer set, letting two people use the same phone but with different camera feeds. Thanks to its design, you can fold iPhone Duo in such a way that the camera stays pointed where you want without being held. You can let iOS monitor the feed, and take the picture when it thinks you're ready. As to the screen, Apple spent a lot of time talking up the engineering that went into minimizing the crease, getting the under-finger feel right, and more. A special coating makes the screen feel closer to glass than the plasticky feel some folding phones have, while also cutting glare and reflections. Nano-scale layers of lenses help the screen stay bright and readable, while reducing the wear of all the folding and unfolding it will undergo during its life. That's not all the engineering that went into iPhone Duo, either. The frame is not only made of titanium, but reinforced at key points with custom materials for added strength. The hinge is weighted, balanced, and carefully structured to fully support the screen at every point of the folding process. You can set the two halves at any angle (up to 180 degrees) and they will stay there. Use it like a small iPad, set one screen at an angle like a laptop while you type on the other one, or make a tent shape, using the phone like a stand while you watch the outer display. The phone will react how you expect, even going so far as to constantly balance the audio coming from its dual speakers based on how the two halves are configured. iOS 27 has been designed to take full advantage of this phone's unique abilities. You can do a lot of the multi-tasking tricks that you can on iPad, such as opening two apps side by side, quickly moving between on-screen apps, showing a list of emails and an open message at once, and more. You can see two home screen pages at once, and your dock is now vertical. Video controls now appear on the side of the screen, rather than the bottom, so videos have more space and so your thumb can reach the controls. The status bar is smaller and now stays in a corner, again, to give apps more room. Apps have new APIs available, letting them, for example, show a list of options on one half of the screen and a preview of the selected option on the other half. iOS will even detect how the phone is being used and move content toward the edge, so it is easier to tap or see. I realize that much of this section has been about cameras, on-screen layouts, and other things that a lot of you reading this won't care about. That's because that was the focus of the presentation. For now, iPhone Duo feels like a device that will be amazing for plenty of sighted users, but will have less appeal to those of us who use VoiceOver. Low vision folks may love the larger screen, but not being such a person myself, I can't really comment on that. Personally, I'm going to see how things go with this phone, play with one in person once my local stores have some, and not worry about getting my own just yet. I don't know if there will be enough advantage for VoiceOver to justify the cost. Of course, it would be nice to have Touch ID again. iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model. As with iPhone 18 Pro, you can increase this all the way to 2TB. Preorders open on October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability starting on October 23. AirPods 5 Today brought us a new AirPods model: AirPods 5 . Like the previous generation, they come in two variants, one more expensive than the other. With AirPods 4, the cheaper model lacked active noise cancelation and wireless charging. That's not the case anymore With this new generation, both variants have ANC. The more expensive AirPods add volume adjustment on the stem, just like AirPods Pro, and a case that supports wireless charging. As we've come to expect, the case can handle MagSafe, Qi, and Apple Watch chargers. The premium version also have a five-hour battery life, which is an hour more than what the less expensive ones offer. This is measured with ANC enabled. Both versions of AirPods 5 are, Apple claims, designed to feel and sound better while lasting longer. ANC is 50% more effective than AirPods 4, while transparency sounds more natural. Audio sounds more detailed and rich, and the earbuds can shrug off more sweat and rain than before. They will also work better in even more ear shapes--so Apple says, anyway. No, they are still not available in any color other than white. The less expensive AirPods cost $129, which is what the non-noise-canceling AirPods 4 cost, and this generation includes ANC. That's a good deal, but for just $20 more, you can get on-stem volume controls and a case that can charge wirelessly. That's $149, which is $30 less expensive than the high-end AirPods 4. Apple isn't known for lowering prices, so this is a very pleasant surprise. You can pre-order starting today (September 9). Deliveries will begin arriving September 18, which is also when stores will start offering the new AirPods. Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 The Apple Watch got some nice enhancements this time around. They all apply equally to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, so I will just talk about the new features here. Everything is true of both models, neither of which seems to have changed, physically, from its predecessor. The first improvement is to the heart sensors. Apple Watch has always used lights to measure your pulse, and that hasn't changed. The LEDs in these new models are different, though. Skin contact is better, the LEDs have been arranged in a ring pattern, and the color of the light has gone from red to green. Add in the new electrical sensors for ECG readings, and Apple Watch has never had a more accurate measure of your heart rate. Almost more exciting is how often Apple Watch now takes heart measurements: every five seconds. This is up to sixty times more often than previous Apple Watches did. Heart rate variability (HRV) is now measured every five minutes, which is a 24 times increase. HRV is an indicator of stress and cardiovascular health, so the more (and more accurate) the readings, the better. This generation of watch has better step length tracking as well, meaning that indoor walks and runs will be measured more accurately than before. Apple also claims that this makes Apple Watch the most accurate step tracker of all the modern wearables. They are therefore adding a step count complication, at long last. What will watchOS do with all this data? Apart from your heart rate complication actually showing your current pulse, Apple has made a series of health data improvements. A readiness score suggests whether you should make today a recovery-focused day or a day during which you can push more. On iPhone, your heart and activity data feed a new Longevity feature. You can see how you are doing over time, how your metrics compare to the average person at your age, and what you could do to improve things. To make this feature more accurate, you can take VO2 max, flexibility, movement, and other tests, all done using your iPhone's cameras and live coaching from the app. You can also purchase bloodwork from Quest for $119, directly through the Health app (U.S. only, for now). The results will inform your health insights and recommendations. You can also connect your existing health records, as has been possible for some time. It's not all about health, though. Audio Intelligence is a set of features centered around the microphones in the watch and Siri AI's increased abilities. All of these features are opt-in, meaning they are not enabled by default. Sound Recognition has been on iPhones for years, but now comes to Apple Watch. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can be alerted to sirens, alarms, doorbells, and other sounds. This works even without iPhone nearby. Live Rewind: double press the digital crown and you get a transcript of the last fifteen seconds of conversation. You can read it, or choose to send it to Siri for further use. During the presentation, they showed a server listing food options, then an Apple Watch user bringing up the list as a transcript. It's not clear if you have to activate this feature each time you want the watch to start paying attention, or if it is always available. Siri Recap is a feature you turn on when you want it, such as during a business meeting or an important conversation. Once the event is over, you turn Recap off again. Siri will generate a title and key points from what it heard, letting you review what was said and jog your memory. I assume this also adds to Siri AI's context, letting you ask questions about what was said in the meeting last week, for instance. Shazam for song detection is nothing new, but it is now automatic (once you turn the feature on). You can always know what song is playing near you, without having to ask Siri to do anything. Apple promised that all of these features run locally or, when they don't, are end-to-end encrypted and have extra security built in. No speakers are ever identified or tagged, no audio is saved, nothing is used for training AI. In fact, audio processed by Apple Watch can't leave the system because of how the S11 SoC is designed. Apple has a whole privacy paper about Audio Intelligence if you want to read more. Speaking of the S11 system, let's go over what we know, which isn't much. We know it has something called an Audio Exclave, which is where audio from the watch's microphones is saved and processed. en.body:
Apple has just wrapped up Surprise and Shine, the big fall announcement event. We got new iPhones, Apple Watches, and (non-pro) AirPods. And yes, the rumors were finally true: one of the new iPhones is a folding one. AirPods have some new tricks, the new Apple Watch has some very nice improvements, and even the normal iPhones are worth checking out. Let's get into it.

All of the iPhones announced today share a few features, so we'll start there.

At the heart of each new iPhone is the A20 Pro, a system on a chip (SoC) that's better than anything Apple has ever made. So said the presenters, anyway. This is Apple's first 2NM chip, which basically means they shrank the parts so they can fit more into the same amount of space, all while using less power and producing less heat. The A20 Pro comes with four efficiency cores and two cores meant to do serious work, which is the same distribution as last year (six cores, with four efficiency and two powerful ones). The big change here is that the two workhorse cores, called super cores, are beefed up considerably. Apple claims they have desktop performance. The graphics chip has also been upgraded, with seven cores and faster access to the phone's RAM; Apple says graphics run up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro.

It's 2026, so we can't not talk about AI, specifically large language models. The A20 Pro has neural accelerators to boost AI performance for the CPU and GPU cores, but the star of the show is the neural engine. Or rather, the engines, plural. Each A20 Pro has two of them, not just one, giving the chip 32 neural cores to work with. Combined with the A20's increased access to memory, Apple said that this is the best chip for mobile AI tasks.

All of this performance is going to produce a lot of heat, so Apple took the vapor chamber from iPhone 17 Pro and made some improvements. The way the chip's components transfer heat to the chamber is more efficient now, the materials have been updated, and the design has been altered. The new design has three times the space and is made from a combination of titanium and a special copper alloy. It transfers 40% more heat than the system on iPhone 17 Pro, letting the phone do more work for longer before it has to slow itself down to keep from overheating.

Remember Siri AI, a version of Siri that is aware of your locations, messages, and other details? It was announced back in June. If you don't follow Apple news as obsessively as I do, the short version is that Siri is far more aware and capable than before. You can ask for "that recipe Jake sent me a couple months ago", you can issue more natural commands, and you can get much more accurate results with dictation. All of this is kept in a new Siri app, so you can check on past conversations. Oh, and Siri's voice is better than ever.

Anyway, Siri AI is fully supported by all the new phones, and Apple spent some time reminding us of what all is going to be possible. There are some extra goodies for Apple Watch Series 12 owners who have Siri AI devices, too, but we'll get to those later.

As has become customary, Apple is offering this year's pro phones in standard and Max variants. The Max has the most battery life of any iPhone ever, while the smaller phone has battery life equivalent to what iPhone 17 Pro Max offers. This seems to be the main difference; both have the same chip, camera, design, and everything else, so I'll just talk about iPhone 18 Pro from here on out. Everything also applies to iPhone 18 Pro Max unless I say otherwise.

The stand-out feature of the camera system this year is variable aperture. Specially-designed, tiny pieces in the camera can move to let in more or less light, which also changes the field depth. The aperture widens in low light, closes some in bright light, and can be manually adjusted to change the feel of a picture. I guess professional photographers will be jumping for joy.

The A20 Pro's AI capabilities also allow Apple to add more camera enhancements, some of which we knew about already from the iOS 27 announcement at WWDC back in June. What is unique to iPhone 18 Pro, though, is a new set of manual camera controls, called pro controls. These let you change the aperture, white balance, and other settings whose purpose I can only guess at. You can even use AI to keep video locked on a subject. But you're not here for camera details, so let's get on with it.

There are a few other, smaller changes compared to iPhone 17 Pro. The new phone can charge faster when plugged in (as opposed to using wireless charging). The Dynamic Island is also smaller and now supports up to three live activities at once.

Surprisingly, that's about it. The battery life improvements are great, the A20 Pro sounds like an impressive chip, and the colors have changed (silver, black, glacier, and burgundy). Aside from that, faster wired charging, and the camera improvements, everything seems to be the same. Apple didn't mention the screen, body material, any new or changed buttons, speakers, wifi performance, or anything else. It seems iPhone 18 Pro is, physically, the same as iPhone 17 Pro, just with a new chip and camera.

You can pre-order iPhone 18 Pro starting September 12, and it will start shipping on September 18. The Pro starts at $1,199, $1,299 for the Pro Max. This gives you 256GB of storage, just like last year. You can upgrade all the way up to 2TB of storage, the first time any iPhone has offered such a large internal drive. Just know that it won't be cheap. You can also check out the new array of colors for Apple's official cases, cross-body straps, and (new this year) wrist straps.

Apple's first entry into the world of foldable phones is called iPhone Duo . It has a 5.4-inch outer display and unfolds to show a 7.6-inch screen. Both screens have full Apple Pencil support, and the outer screen has Ceramic Shield 2. The frame is high-grade titanium, colored either white or night sky. The side button acts how you expect, but also sports a Touch ID sensor--the phone lacks Face ID. You can add multiple fingers, so that no matter how you happen to hold the phone, the finger resting on the button can unlock it. You can also unlock your phone with your watch. Also, despite being foldable, iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating. That means dust and water will have a hard time getting into it, but you shouldn't take it swimming.

Each half of iPhone Duo is very, very thin--after all, the whole package has to be comfortably thin when folded. Apple says that each half is the thinnest iPhone ever produced, which suggests that the halves are thinner than an iPhone Air. Despite this, iPhone Duo has good battery life (30 hours of video playback on the internal screen, 44 when using the outer one) and supports fast wired charging. It also, as mentioned earlier, has the same A20 Pro chip and vapor chamber cooling as iPhone 18 Pro. It even has Apple's custom cellular modem, the C2, giving it millimeter wave 5G support (U.S. only for now) and faster and more efficient cellular communications overall.

The camera situation is interesting. iPhone Duo sports the same camera system as iPhone 18 Pro, though without the variable aperture feature. When unfolded, an under-screen selfie camera is available, while a more capable camera lives just above the outer screen. This enables some neat options, such as letting both the photographer and the subject see the camera feed (one person on the inner screen, the other on the outer one) before a picture is taken. If you are taking pictures of children, iOS lets you enable animations designed to draw attention and get the kids' eyes looking toward the lens. When making FaceTime calls, someone can use the inner camera and screen, while someone else can use the outer set, letting two people use the same phone but with different camera feeds. Thanks to its design, you can fold iPhone Duo in such a way that the camera stays pointed where you want without being held. You can let iOS monitor the feed, and take the picture when it thinks you're ready.

As to the screen, Apple spent a lot of time talking up the engineering that went into minimizing the crease, getting the under-finger feel right, and more. A special coating makes the screen feel closer to glass than the plasticky feel some folding phones have, while also cutting glare and reflections. Nano-scale layers of lenses help the screen stay bright and readable, while reducing the wear of all the folding and unfolding it will undergo during its life.

That's not all the engineering that went into iPhone Duo, either. The frame is not only made of titanium, but reinforced at key points with custom materials for added strength. The hinge is weighted, balanced, and carefully structured to fully support the screen at every point of the folding process. You can set the two halves at any angle (up to 180 degrees) and they will stay there. Use it like a small iPad, set one screen at an angle like a laptop while you type on the other one, or make a tent shape, using the phone like a stand while you watch the outer display. The phone will react how you expect, even going so far as to constantly balance the audio coming from its dual speakers based on how the two halves are configured.

iOS 27 has been designed to take full advantage of this phone's unique abilities. You can do a lot of the multi-tasking tricks that you can on iPad, such as opening two apps side by side, quickly moving between on-screen apps, showing a list of emails and an open message at once, and more. You can see two home screen pages at once, and your dock is now vertical. Video controls now appear on the side of the screen, rather than the bottom, so videos have more space and so your thumb can reach the controls. The status bar is smaller and now stays in a corner, again, to give apps more room. Apps have new APIs available, letting them, for example, show a list of options on one half of the screen and a preview of the selected option on the other half. iOS will even detect how the phone is being used and move content toward the edge, so it is easier to tap or see.

I realize that much of this section has been about cameras, on-screen layouts, and other things that a lot of you reading this won't care about. That's because that was the focus of the presentation. For now, iPhone Duo feels like a device that will be amazing for plenty of sighted users, but will have less appeal to those of us who use VoiceOver. Low vision folks may love the larger screen, but not being such a person myself, I can't really comment on that. Personally, I'm going to see how things go with this phone, play with one in person once my local stores have some, and not worry about getting my own just yet. I don't know if there will be enough advantage for VoiceOver to justify the cost. Of course, it would be nice to have Touch ID again.

iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model. As with iPhone 18 Pro, you can increase this all the way to 2TB. Preorders open on October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability starting on October 23.

Today brought us a new AirPods model: AirPods 5 . Like the previous generation, they come in two variants, one more expensive than the other. With AirPods 4, the cheaper model lacked active noise cancelation and wireless charging. That's not the case anymore

With this new generation, both variants have ANC. The more expensive AirPods add volume adjustment on the stem, just like AirPods Pro, and a case that supports wireless charging. As we've come to expect, the case can handle MagSafe, Qi, and Apple Watch chargers. The premium version also have a five-hour battery life, which is an hour more than what the less expensive ones offer. This is measured with ANC enabled.

Both versions of AirPods 5 are, Apple claims, designed to feel and sound better while lasting longer. ANC is 50% more effective than AirPods 4, while transparency sounds more natural. Audio sounds more detailed and rich, and the earbuds can shrug off more sweat and rain than before. They will also work better in even more ear shapes--so Apple says, anyway. No, they are still not available in any color other than white.

The less expensive AirPods cost $129, which is what the non-noise-canceling AirPods 4 cost, and this generation includes ANC. That's a good deal, but for just $20 more, you can get on-stem volume controls and a case that can charge wirelessly. That's $149, which is $30 less expensive than the high-end AirPods 4. Apple isn't known for lowering prices, so this is a very pleasant surprise. You can pre-order starting today (September 9). Deliveries will begin arriving September 18, which is also when stores will start offering the new AirPods.

The Apple Watch got some nice enhancements this time around. They all apply equally to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, so I will just talk about the new features here. Everything is true of both models, neither of which seems to have changed, physically, from its predecessor.

The first improvement is to the heart sensors. Apple Watch has always used lights to measure your pulse, and that hasn't changed. The LEDs in these new models are different, though. Skin contact is better, the LEDs have been arranged in a ring pattern, and the color of the light has gone from red to green. Add in the new electrical sensors for ECG readings, and Apple Watch has never had a more accurate measure of your heart rate.

Almost more exciting is how often Apple Watch now takes heart measurements: every five seconds. This is up to sixty times more often than previous Apple Watches did. Heart rate variability (HRV) is now measured every five minutes, which is a 24 times increase. HRV is an indicator of stress and cardiovascular health, so the more (and more accurate) the readings, the better.

This generation of watch has better step length tracking as well, meaning that indoor walks and runs will be measured more accurately than before. Apple also claims that this makes Apple Watch the most accurate step tracker of all the modern wearables. They are therefore adding a step count complication, at long last.

What will watchOS do with all this data? Apart from your heart rate complication actually showing your current pulse, Apple has made a series of health data improvements. A readiness score suggests whether you should make today a recovery-focused day or a day during which you can push more.

To make this feature more accurate, you can take VO2 max, flexibility, movement, and other tests, all done using your iPhone's cameras and live coaching from the app. You can also purchase bloodwork from Quest for $119, directly through the Health app (U.S. only, for now). The results will inform your health insights and recommendations. You can also connect your existing health records, as has been possible for some time.

It's not all about health, though. Audio Intelligence is a set of features centered around the microphones in the watch and Siri AI's increased abilities. All of these features are opt-in, meaning they are not enabled by default.

Sound Recognition has been on iPhones for years, but now comes to Apple Watch. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can be alerted to sirens, alarms, doorbells, and other sounds. This works even without iPhone nearby.

Live Rewind: double press the digital crown and you get a transcript of the last fifteen seconds of conversation. You can read it, or choose to send it to Siri for further use. During the presentation, they showed a server listing food options, then an Apple Watch user bringing up the list as a transcript. It's not clear if you have to activate this feature each time you want the watch to start paying attention, or if it is always available.

Siri Recap is a feature you turn on when you want it, such as during a business meeting or an important conversation. Once the event is over, you turn Recap off again. Siri will generate a title and key points from what it heard, letting you review what was said and jog your memory. I assume this also adds to Siri AI's context, letting you ask questions about what was said in the meeting last week, for instance.

Shazam for song detection is nothing new, but it is now automatic (once you turn the feature on). You can always know what song is playing near you, without having to ask Siri to do anything.

Apple promised that all of these features run locally or, when they don't, are end-to-end encrypted and have extra security built in. No speakers are ever identified or tagged, no audio is saved, nothing is used for training AI. In fact, audio processed by Apple Watch can't leave the system because of how the S11 SoC is designed. en.body:
The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part.

Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features provided no speech or braille. This affected the JAWS Results Viewer, OCR Viewer, Picture Smart, and Message Center, along with New Outlook and Microsoft Copilot 365.

On September 6 we deployed a temporary change to JAWS so that customers would not have to wait while the underlying problem was still being investigated. On September 7 Microsoft released an update that corrected the root cause. Because that update resolves the problem at its source, we have since removed our temporary change.

The Microsoft update is delivered automatically, so there is nothing for you to install or turn on. The temporary work-around we shared last week, toggling the Touch Cursor off and on, is no longer needed.

If you are still experiencing the problem, please restart your computer so the Microsoft update can take effect. If that does not resolve it, please contact your local dealer or our technical support team.

We appreciate everyone who reported this to us and who let us know when things began working again. Those reports helped us confirm the cause quickly and gave us what we needed to work with Microsoft toward a resolution.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2 with Fix for Problems Downloading Updates over Cellular Connections
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2, bringing a fix for an issue that prevented users from downloading updates over cellular connections. As iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2 were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a specific issue, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 26.6.2 This update fixes an issue that prevents downloading a software update over a cellular connection. iPadOS 26.6.2 This update fixes an issue that prevents downloading a software update over a cellular connection. How to Update iOS and iPadOS 26.6.2 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: In-Process 8th September 2026
en.summary: It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new: NVDA 2026.2 Magnifier A new Beta already? Resetting to Factory Defaults NVDA 2026.2 NVDA 2026.2 has been released! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.… Read More
en.body:
It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new:

NVDA 2026.2 has been released ! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.

The Magnifier provides zoom and color filtering options to assist users with visual impairments. The Magnifier currently only supports full screen mode, with docked modes planned in a future release. Touch support has been significantly expanded with new pinch gestures and touch-based browse mode navigation for web content. You can now navigate between links, headings, form fields, and other elements using touch flicks.

Speech features have been enhanced with support for custom speech dictionaries that can be provided by add-ons and new dictionary entry types for more granular control. A new voice setting for OneCore voices was added to control pauses after punctuation. A new command allows repeating the last spoken information, with the ability to display it in a browsable message. The default gesture to repeat the last spoken information is NVDA+x , which can be changed in the Input Gestures dialog.

The braille display can now automatically scroll, and DotPad devices support multi-button combinations. The default gesture to toggle automatic scroll is NVDA+alt+k .

Liblouis has been updated with new Italian and Estonian braille tables. When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration.

Download the new version from the NVDA 2026.2 release post (or by checking for updates from within NVDA).

As well as the article below, and a new extensive section on the magnifier in the User Guide, our “Basic Training for NVDA” module has been updated with a number of updates. Of particular interest is a new section on the magnifier, there is also a topic covering reading the last spoken information and other new and improved content. These new updates are currently only available in the electronic text version. You can purchase Basic Training for NVDA from our shop . If you have already purchased the module, you can download the new version with the Magnifier section from the downloads page after logging into your NV Access account .

We are very excited to incorporate a magnifier into NVDA for the first time. We have had a lot of comments from users who are excited for this feature, and we’ve had some questions too, so let’s cover off some of the things it can and cannot do, and why it is a useful addition to NVDA:

First Release Firstly, it’s worth highlighting that this is the first release of NVDA with a magnifier and so the features will improve over time. We try to ship NVDA features incrementally, keeping the initial design scope small and allowing for early user feedback. This allows us to grow the magnifier in response to user reaction. Currently NVDA only works as a full-screen magnifier. We plan to extend the options in future releases. Adding windowed / docked modes is a high priority once bugs are addressed and the full-screen mode is more polished.

What CAN the magnifier do? The magnifier has most of the features you might expect from such a feature: You can zoom in and out (from 1x up to 50x) The view will follow the mouse, keyboard focus, browse mode focus and NVDA navigator object and review cursor – user selectable You can pan the view with the keyboard, in configurable increments, or jump to the edges of the screen You can adjust the colours (normal, inverted or greyscale) You can choose how objects are tracked (Centred or relative to their position on screen) You can configure the keystrokes for the various functions There is a keystroke to briefly zoom out and show an overview of the screen

We have made a short demo of the magnification feature on our YouTube channel .

Should I change magnifiers? Particularly if you currently use another magnification solution, we very much encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier. We are interested in your feedback, and particularly where you would like to see our feature improve.

If you already use Windows magnifier or another program, you can keep using it and it will continue to work with NVDA’s speech functions. Just as we don’t recommend having two screen readers running at once, we also wouldn’t recommend having NVDA’s magnifier AND another magnifier running at the same time.

If you do currently use Windows Magnifier, some of the reasons you may consider NVDA’s magnifier: It starts when NVDA starts (once you enable it) Configurable keystrokes Greyscale colour filtering mode Relative tracking mode Ability to follow NVDA’s object navigation and review cursor Keys to jump to edges of screen No settings window always on screen Ability to set your desired settings once and save to a portable copy you can use on any computer

If you use Windows magnifier in docked or lens mode, or some of the other features which haven’t yet made it into the NVDA magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, then you may wish to stay with Windows magnifier for now – but we do encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier and let us know what you think.

Before we even got this edition of In-Process finished, to tell you all about 2026.2…. we ALREADY have a new beta? Of NVDA 2026.3 ? Yep! And I’m not going to talk about that yet – if you want to check it out, please head to the beta release announcement . What I did want to briefly mention, was how we came to have a new beta out, when the paint isn’t even dry on NVDA 2026.2?

Great question! And it comes down to how we develop software. Both our internal developers, and the community are constantly working on improving features, fixing bugs, and adding new things into NVDA. As a new piece of code gets incorporated into NVDA, it goes into an “Alpha” build – an early pre-release build with whatever has been changed recently. This lets our developers and our most dedicated testers try it out and give feedback. These come out almost daily (and sometimes several in one day). Because of the quick turnaround, we don’t share them on social media or here on the blog, but if you’d like to try them out, alpha builds are publicly available from the snapshots page . Be aware that they may not be as polished as the stable releases – though the process to test them out is identical.

So, generally a week after a stable release, we collate all the things which have been in alpha for at least a couple of weeks, and put them together into a “beta” release of the next version. While we may still have some features we are working on for later betas, as well any regressions or major issues discovered from the previous release, we can turn much of our development attention on towards the NEXT release.

So, if you ever find an issue with NVDA, the sooner you let us know, the sooner we can prioritise it and work on a fix as needed.

One of the perhaps less glamourous updates in NVDA 2026.2 is to a feature you hopefully don’t ever need to use.

“When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration”

We’ve covered resetting NVDA to factory defaults previously , though it is worth being aware of. While something you hopefully don’t need, if you ever DO need it, it’s good to know it exists. With this new change, if you reset NVDA to factory defaults, a dialog appears advising “Your configuration has been reset to factory defaults. Choose OK to keep factory defaults, or Undo to restore your previous configuration”. This could be useful just in case you ever inadvertently activate the wrong item on the NVDA menu for instance, and may hopefully save you from needing go through setting up NVDA to your preferences again.

That’s all for this week, do update to NVDA 2026.2 if you haven’t already, and we’d love to hear your feedback on the new features – the magnifier of course, but also the other updates.

Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. es.title: Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 288e684536edb011710d760fc18ba7b652241085742e304e17d8ee01ede2d20f. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.body:
A recent Microsoft update is changing how accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS may not receive the information it needs from these applications, causing some features to provide no speech or braille.

This may affect:

The issue is not currently observed in web browsers such as Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

If you find that JAWS is not working as expected in web-based apps, toggle the Touch Cursor on and off again for JAWS to resume speaking normally. To enable the Touch Cursor, press SHIFT+NUM PAD PLUS if using Desktop keyboard layout and CAPS LOCK+SHIFT+SEMICOLON if using Laptop keyboard layout. To toggle it off and return to the Virtual PC Cursor, press NUM PAD PLUS twice quickly (in Desktop layout) or hold CAPS LOCK and press SEMICOLON twice quickly in Laptop layout.

If the content still does not respond as expected, press F5 to refresh the page or application content.

Vispero is working directly with Microsoft to investigate the issue and determine the appropriate fix. We will provide additional information when it becomes available.

Si recuerdas el anuncio de la beta 7 de NVDA 2026.2 , vino acompañado de una mala noticia: el fallecimiento de Rui Fontes, miembro muy activo de la comunidad a nivel internacional y propietario de Tiflotecnia, la compañía que actualmente comercializa las voces más recientes de Vocalizer para NVDA. Tras este triste anuncio, la venta de las voces quedó en pausa, a la espera de que se aclarase la situación en Tiflotecnia. Desde NVDA.es nos complace anunciar que dicha aclaración ya ha tenido lugar, y por tanto volvemos a reactivar la venta de este sintetizador de voz rápido y de alta calidad. En consecuencia, ya puedes volver a adquirir licencias completas por 90 euros, y actualizaciones de licencias de la versión 3 a la 4 por 50 euros, en ambos casos con impuestos incluidos. Recuerda que cada licencia te permitirá usar el sintetizador en hasta tres equipos de forma simultánea. Si vas a formatear o quieres hacer cambios relevantes de hardware, puedes devolver tu licencia al servidor para recuperarla más adelante. Además, es posible activar y desactivar licencias en equipos que no disponen de conexión a Internet, algo que con la versión 3.0 no se podía hacer. Y por si fuera poco, una sola licencia incluye todas las voces disponibles, ¡en todos los idiomas y con todas las calidades! Si todavía no lo has hecho, puedes instalar y probar estas voces sin coste alguno durante una semana. Te animamos a hacerlo, ¡la experiencia merece la pena! ¡Hasta la próxima!

en.title: BlindGram
en.summary: blindGram is an independent accessible Telegram client for blind and low-vision Android users, based on Telegram’s open-source Android code. Its optional blindGram Assistant reads text…
en.body:
blindGram is an independent accessible Telegram client for blind and low-vision Android users, based on Telegram’s open-source Android code.

Its optional blindGram Assistant reads text inside images, provides offline image labels, and converts voice messages and round videos to text offline in 23 languages without Telegram Premium.

Optional AI features provide detailed image descriptions, summaries, follow-up questions, and questions about any message through the user’s own OpenRouter, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or compatible provider. AI features remain off until enabled.

Website: https://en.blindgram.ir/

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Designed specifically for blind and low-vision users . Interface and message actions are optimized for screen-reader navigation, with primary testing using TalkBack .

Assistant results open in accessible dialogs or conversation screens where text can be read, selected, and copied.

Offline OCR , image labels, and voice-to-text require no account or Telegram Premium.

AI features are optional and clearly disclose when content leaves the device.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

BlindGram 15.0; Supports Android 5.0 and newer;

es.summary: Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de magnificador integrado, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y una ampliación de funciones de voz y braille. El magnificador ofrece opciones de aumentos y de filtrado de colores para ayudar a los usuarios con discapacidad visual. Actualmente, el Magnificador solo es compatible con el modo a pantalla completa, aunque en una futura actualización se prevé la incorporación de modos acoplados. Se ha ampliado considerablemente la compatibilidad táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizco y la navegación por el contenido web mediante el modo táctil. Ahora puedes desplazarte entre enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos mediante gestos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con la compatibilidad con diccionarios de voz personalizados que pueden proporcionarse mediante complementos, así como con nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que permiten un control más preciso. Se ha añadido una nueva configuración de voz para las voces de OneCore con el fin de controlar las pausas tras los signos de puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la posibilidad de mostrarla en un mensaje que se pueda leer. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información leída en voz alta es NVDA+x, que se puede modificar en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Ahora, la pantalla braille puede desplazarse automáticamente y los dispositivos DotPad admiten combinaciones de varios botones. El atajo predeterminado para activar o desactivar el desplazamiento automático es NVDA+Alt+k. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas de braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer las opciones predeterminadas de fábrica de NVDA, ahora hay disponible un botón «Deshacer» para recuperar la configuración anterior. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.2, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.2, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es f3f8d29974a88d687b3c4809be192219ec579c5bdabcda5aaf53635288bca824. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc2, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

Web accessibility is crucial to ensure screen reader users can readily access information on the web. This includes content such as:

en.body:
Welcome to JAWS Jumpstart, a four-week series designed to help students, teachers, new users, and anyone looking for a refresher get the most out of JAWS as the new school year begins. Each Monday in August, we’ll share a practical tip, shortcut, or feature to help you start the year off on the right foot. This week, we’re sharing JAWS customization tips to help you improve productivity and efficiency.

Customizing JAWS enables you to tailor specific settings like speech rate, verbosity, and punctuation to meet your needs. Customization also helps you optimize JAWS for specific applications or tasks, improving efficiency and productivity in your daily work or studies. Here are three tips for customizing JAWS.

Customizing speech settings is important because it ensures JAWS communicates information in a way that is clear, comfortable, and easy for you to understand. To customize speech settings:

PlaceMarkers in JAWS let you mark specific spots on web pages, documents, or emails so you can quickly return to them later. Temporary PlaceMarkers are for one-time use during your current session, while permanent PlaceMarkers are saved and available whenever you revisit the page or document. PlaceMarkers are helpful for navigating long or complex content, making it easier to find important information or start and end text selections.

To create a PlaceMarker:

To return to a PlaceMarker, use CTRL+SHIFT+K to open the PlaceMarkers List and select the marker you want. You can also press K to navigate to PlaceMarkers on a web page.

Using PlaceMarkers helps you efficiently navigate and manage information in large documents or web pages.

You can now save your JAWS settings to the cloud and access them on any computer where you sign in with your Vispero account. This makes it much easier to keep your setup consistent without having to reconfigure JAWS each time. This also ensures your customizations remain safely stored and in situations where your current computer becomes unusable.

With Cloud Settings, you can sync:

These settings will be saved to the cloud so you can sync them on multiple computers. This also makes it easier to restore your settings on a new device.

This feature is only available in regions where Vispero accounts are supported. This feature is also a part of our Early Adopter Program, so you can try it out and provide feedback before it is fully released.

To enable it in the Early Adopter Program and sync your settings:

To learn more about PlaceMarkers or additional ways to customize your JAWS settings, watch or download these archived trainings:

en.title: In-Process 24th August 2026
en.summary: We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around: NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! Automatically Scrolling the Braille Display Getting help from others New Unassigned Commands Finding out more about what is new NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all… Read More
en.body:
We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around:

The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all users to download this RC and provide feedback. Unless any critical bugs are found, this will be identical to the final 2026.2 release.

NVDA 2026.2 includes:

Magnifier (full screen, colour filtering, zoom, focus tracking) Improved touch gestures (links, form fields, etc) NVDA+x to repeat last spoken information Improved speech dictionaries Automatic Braille Display scrolling & much more!

We would encourage you to try out the NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate , especially if you haven’t yet tried any of the betas. You can do this by creating a portable copy or by selecting “Continue running” from the launcher, to run a temporary copy and not interfere with your installed copy of NVDA.

One of the new features in NVDA 2026.2, is that we: “Added the ability to automatically scroll the braille display”. This comes courtesy of Noelia, one of our prominent Spanish contributors. Reading the user guide entry for the new “Automatic scroll rate” feature, it notes:

Automatic braille scrolling can be enabled to scroll the display at a set speed. When using this feature, the braille display scrolls to present information which is more than will fit on the display at once. The feature is disabled by default. You can change the gestures assigned to use automatic braille scrolling in NVDA’s Input Gestures dialog before it can be used. Gestures are also available to speed up or slow down the rate of automatic scrolling. Alternatively, you can set the automatic scroll rate in Braille Settings.

While braille is scrolling, you can still use the scroll back and scroll forward commands without stopping scrolling. Scroll back can be useful to read previous contents again. Scroll forward can be useful to skip a blank line, or if the line being read is short.

While reading, automatic braille scrolling will stop when any of the following happen:

The toggle automatic braille scrolling key is pressed The user presses a key or gesture which would display a new message The focus is moved (including with braille display panning keys) The end of the document is reached The state of the lock or secure screen is changed (such as the computer being locked)

The commands for this feature are: Toggle automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+k Increase automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+L Decrease automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+j

Last fortnight, we covered ways you can get help from within NVDA itself. This time around, let’s have a look at some of the places you can get help from others. As with last fortnight’s post, this list covers getting help for NVDA itself only, aimed at end users: NV Access Telephone Support : If you’ve still got questions after following last fortnight’s tips and reading Basic Training for NVDA etc, give us a call. Telephone support IS a paid service, and for end-user support only, but it is available 24/7. We have numbers you can call in Australia or the USA, OR you can email us and we can call you anywhere in the world. You also get telephone support included with the NVDA Productivity Bundle . Official NVDA Email Group : While we monitor various other groups, the one place you know you will find NV Access staff, and users, is the official, friendly, NVDA email group at https://nvaccess.org/nvda-users – plus, as a free, welcoming and popular resource, you will often get help from other users even quicker than we can respond. Local language email groups : We have a huge list of email groups in many languages. Know of a group which isn’t listed? Please, let us know so we can share it on the connect page for others! Social media : Our community on Mastodon is the most active, but you can also find us on Facebook and other platforms . NVDA Remote Access : Have a friend who can help with your PC? You can let them connect to your PC to help you. Note there are a number of security measures in place to ensure this feature can only be accessed by deliberate action from both parties.

For the upcoming NVDA 2026.2, we’ve added a couple of new “unassigned” commands. These aren’t always the most obvious to find, so I thought it was worth highlighting them here: Added an unassigned command to toggle keyboard layout. ( #19211 , @CyrilleB79 ) Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z ) Added an unassigned command to report the current status of the Screen Curtain. ( #19759 )

Commands like these can provide useful functionality, but may often only be required by some users. As we are all aware, screen readers already have a lot of keystrokes, so we always have to think carefully before assigning new keystrokes.

For instance, the toggle keyboard layout setting. Most users will setup the keyboard layout how they prefer, and never need to change it. For the rare time you may wish to change it, the setting is on the keyboard settings page, which is available with NVDA+control+k . For testing or teaching, a command to toggle the layout on the fly may be invaluable, so, in NVDA 2026.2, it’s there if you need it.

In any NVDA release announcement , there is a link to “ What’s new in this release of NVDA ” (I’ve linked to those to things for NVDA 2026.2 RC1). That document gives a summary of the highlights in several paragraphs, and then bullet points for all the changes in groups: Important notes : information such as older Windows versions no longer supported Security fixes : Updates to NVDA which fix potential security issues. New features : New functionality in NVDA. For instance, NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information, or the ability to automatically scroll the braille display Changes : Features which may be slightly different, such as renaming the “COM Registration Fixing Tool” to “System Accessibility Repair Tool”. Bug fixes : Fixing features which didn’t work the way they should. For instance, in NVDA 2026.2, we’ve fixed a crash in the add-on store, NVDA now recovers quicker from freezes in some applications, and form controls are correctly reported in Firefox again. Changes for developers : Updates which may affect how contributors code for NVDA. These don’t affect end users directly. For instance, updating the version of Python used, or new functions developers can call to find out information. Deprecations : Again, only for developers, function calls which either no longer work, or have been changed to something else, and developers should transition over to the new function call.

In most of the bullet points for each release, there is a number at the end, and sometimes a username. For instance, in the unassigned commands article above: “Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z )”

In this case, #17005 is the issue number assigned to the original request for this feature. @tareh7z is the GitHub user who wrote the code and submitted the pull request to fix it – thanks @tareh7z! And thanks to ALL our contributors. NVDA 2026.2 is a big release with a lot of amazing features the community have put a lot of work into!

The line in the changes document will hopefully give enough information to quickly describe the feature for most users. The user guide will also have been updated with any relevant information. In this case, look at section 6.1.3 “Other Navigation Commands”, which talks about not only sliders, but other quick navigation commands which don’t have default keystrokes.

The issue number is a link back to that issue, which can be helpful if you’d like to look back at the conversation which prompted the new feature. For instance, in this case, there was some discussion around what other types of information could potentially be accessed with a “slider” command (others that were suggested were ruled out in this case).

That’s all for this time. Do please try out the NVDA 2026.2 release candidate , and of course, let us know of any issues you encounter with it. Next time around we will have more on NVDA 2026.2!

es.title: Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.2. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de ampliación, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y capacidades mejoradas de voz y braille. El ampliador proporciona opciones de zoom y filtro de color para asistir a usuarios con baja visión. Actualmente, el ampliador sólo soporta el modo a pantalla completa, dejando los modos acoplados planificados para una futura versión. Se ha expandido significativamente el soporte táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizcar y con navegación en modo exploración táctil en contenido web. Ahora se puede navegar por enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos usando deslizamientos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con soporte de diccionarios del habla personalizados que pueden proporcionarse en complementos y nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que proporcionan un control más granular. Se ha añadido una nueva opción en las voces OneCore para controlar las pausas después de la puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la capacidad de mostrarla en un mensaje explorable. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información verbalizada es NVDA+x, y se puede cambiar desde el diálogo Gestos de entrada. La pantalla braille ahora puede desplazarse automáticamente, y los dispositivos DotPad soportan combinaciones multibotón. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer NVDA a los valores de fábrica, ahora hay disponible un botón de deshacer para restaurar la configuración anterior. Para instalar esta candidata a liberación, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.2 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 09dfba7e03f37598a50e8495370a063864acd4de48ce6ebdf9ee320c536803f5. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
